analysis.answer: Under current law, an eligible person 21 or older may carry a concealed handgun without a permit. The measure changes this by requiring individuals to obtain a permit from their county sheriff to carry a concealed handgun.
Current law does not require safety training to carry a concealed handgun. The measure adds a requirement to complete an eight-hour safety course in order to obtain the newly required permit.

Applicants will incur the direct financial cost of taking an eight-hour safety course and the opportunity cost of their time. County sheriffs will incur administrative costs to process permit applications and verify training completion.

Individuals seeking to carry a concealed handgun bear the financial and time costs of the permit and training requirements. Instructors who provide firearm safety courses will benefit from a captive market of permit applicants.

Some individuals who currently carry a concealed handgun may choose to stop carrying rather than go through the application process and pay for the safety course. Others may choose to carry openly instead, assuming open carry remains permitless.
The text implies a problem with untrained individuals carrying concealed firearms. It addresses this by making an eight-hour safety course a prerequisite for obtaining a concealed carry permit.

County sheriffs gain the administrative role of processing and issuing concealed carry permits, although their discretion is limited because they "shall issue" the permit to applicants who meet the criteria.
